chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who shot game while it was on a mountain or a wall, and the arrow pierced it, causing it to die.
He said: 'Eat from it, and if water from your shot entered it and it died, do not eat from it.'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said - and there is no slaughter (dhakāh) except in the throat.

key_terms.اَلشَّيْخُ: The Sheikh (referring to al-Tusi or al-Majlisi depending on context, here likely al-Tusi in Tahdhib)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game shot by an arrow if it dies from the wound or blood loss?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of hunting game shot by an arrow, distinguishing between death by the projectile's force versus death by suffocation or blood loss from the wound. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the primary cause of death for determining halal status, while Sheikh al-Tusi’s note reinforces the foundational requirement of severing the throat (hulqum) for ritual slaughter, linking hunting mechanics to broader dietary laws.
